summary: Azraq presented two papers (obj-ship-log-wreck and obj-folio-map) as proof and set them on a crate aboard the Qitaf, then fastened a peri amulet (obj-peri-amulet) to Amina, binding her to a mission to steal the spindle from Isle Jarrah (s-001).

Azraq presented two artifacts (obj-ship-log-wreck and obj-folio-map) as proof aboard the Qitaf and fastened obj-peri-amulet to Amina, binding her to a mission to steal the spindle from Isle Jarrah (s-001).

Azraq explained the Peri Council's demand for 'a single spindle' from Isle Jarrah, stated the Council's motives are urgent but not disclosed, warned that refusal "will be answered" by covenantal consequences, and named possible counters to the amulet (strong mortal will, witches' craft, or use of the Spindle under island terms). Quotes and provenance: s-002.

Azraq explained that the Peri Council wants 'a single spindle' from Isle Jarrah, asserted their motives are urgent but opaque, warned that refusal 'will be answered' by covenantal consequences, and named possible counters to the peri amulet (strong mortal will, witches' craft, or using the Spindle under island terms). (Provenance: s-002).

Amina called the crew, announced the Peri Council's commission to fetch the Spindle from Isle Jarrah, and the Qitaf's crew made departure preparations: canvas lashed, lines checked, hold stowed, lanterns trimmed and hung, bilge run, anchor windlass oiled. The Qitaf then cast off from Port Aden (provenance: s-003).

s-004: Amina procured supplies in the market (oil, wax, line, bitter herbs) and the Qitaf crew examined the folio-map and wreck log aboard ship. The folio showed heavy handling: "The folio had been handled so much that the coastline had gone soft where hands had smudged it; there were crosses darkened into blurs and pencil lines that started with confidence and ended in a scrawl." The wreck log was torn and smudged: "The wreck log lay beside the folio, folded smaller and worse for the sea. The diagram in it had been eaten by a torn edge; what was left looked like a hand that had tried to keep something from going away. Words bled at their margins; an attempt at a phrase had been scrubbed to a smudge and the paper had the desperate weight of a man who had run out of time." Crew traded fragmentary sailor lore: e.g. "Men who left and never found the sea again," and "Reefs that move when you ain't looking. Lights that call a man off his course." Yusuf hid the folio under his jacket and ran navigation checks at the binnacle; Rasim received bitter herbs and, amid a cough, dropped a coin which Yusuf recovered. The Qitaf's stores were made ready (canvas lashed, lanterns trimmed, ropes checked). (Provenance: s-004).

s-005: At first light the Qitaf departed Port Aden bound for Isle Jarrah. During the voyage Azraq stood aft watching the crew with 'silver eyes'; when Amina met his gaze the peri amulet at her throat thrumed ('a thin, precise thrum that ran like a wire from skin to bone'). The folio and wreck log were present aboard the Qitaf and consulted during the passage (see s-004 physical-condition notes). Yusuf kept the folio close under his coat and hid it in a pocket while checking navigation; Rasim's cough persisted and manifested as frailty during the voyage. (Provenance: s-005).

s-006 observed anomalies and seamanship response: The ship encountered a sea-fold. Instrument anomalies occurred: "The compass needle spent a breath where it had been still, then trembled and wandered like a thirsty thing. Binnacle glass went white and then clear as if someone had exhaled between us and the world. The chronometer on the rail juddered; its second hand missed, caught, and then stuttered on as if time itself had hiccuped." The folio and wreck log were consulted and correlated with the sea: "The jagged fold in the water matched the torn diagram I'd smoothed from the wreck log." "When he did, the smudged crosses fell under our course like a second chart: the little dark Xs lined where the sea folded, exactly where my hands felt the deck dip." Crew seamanship actions taken: "I eased a sheet, shifted a coil of chain to starboard, and told Rasim to steer to the swell with his ear more than his eye." A piece of flotsam (a hand's-breadth of wood) bobbled past the hull and was observed and carried off by the fold (forward hook to s-007): "Then, a hand's-breadth of wood—salt-soft, heat-scrambled, flecked with old black tar—bobbled against our hull and scraped past." Rasim's cough worsened during these anomalies (provenance: s-006).
